equipment.name: Adjustable Weight Bench
equipment.notes: CONFIRMED BY THE OWNER: this bench DOES reach a true DECLINE (head below hips), not incline-only. Decline pressing, decline flyes and decline abdominal work are all performable, with the front leg rollers anchoring the legs. Bench1000 PRO FITNESS. Backrest and seat adjust independently through flat, incline and decline. The front leg attachment is FIXED — the rollers do not pivot or lever, so this bench CANNOT do leg extensions or leg curls. The rollers exist only to anchor the legs in decline positions. Knee isolation stays on bands.

equipment.name: Hyperextension bench
equipment.notes: A hyperextension bench or Roman chair. The back pad appears adjustable for height, and the foot rollers are fixed. The angle of the main frame seems to be fixed, providing a decline angle.
A black flat weight bench with a black upholstered pad. The brand "CAP" is visible on the side of the pad. It appears to be in good condition. The bench has a stable H-shaped base.
equipment.name: Flat weight bench

equipment.notes: A pair of yellow parallel dip bars with black foam grips. They appear to be fixed height and stable, suitable for bodyweight exercises.
equipment.name: Parallel dip bars

equipment.notes: Pair of adjustable dumbbells, TRULAP, 8.5 lb to 92 lb per hand. TWO HARD LIMITS, confirmed by the owner: (1) the handles are ROUND-BODIED and ROLL under load — they are NOT a stable base for any bodyweight movement, so never prescribe push-ups, planks, renegade rows or any hold that puts bodyweight through them; (2) 8.5 lb is the LOWEST notch, which is too heavy for light prehab work — rotator-cuff external rotation, scaption, W-raises and similar belong on bands, not on these.
equipment.name: Adjustable dumbbells on stand
Resistance bands
equipment.notes: TWO KINDS, both on hand. (1) LOOP BANDS — a 4-band set of flat continuous loops, 208 cm round, 3 mm thick, colour-coded by strength: YELLOW 0.64 cm (20 lb label), RED 1.3 cm (35 lb), BLACK 2.1 cm (65 lb), PURPLE 3.2 cm (85 lb). The labels are the vendor MAXIMUM and these are 3 mm rather than the usual 4.5 mm, so every band runs LIGHTER than its number — treat the colour as the unit, not the pounds. ALWAYS name the colour when prescribing a band exercise; the bands themselves are not printed with any weight. (2) OLDER TUBE BANDS with handles and a door anchor. Both can loop around the basement post, so the anchor can sit at ANY height. DELIBERATELY NARROW ROLE, confirmed by the owner: dumbbells are ALWAYS preferred when they can do the job, so bands are NOT used for pressing, rowing, pulldowns, curls, pushdowns or wrist work — the dumbbells and the pull-up bar cover all of those. Bands are kept for exactly two things they alone can do: (a) light prehab BELOW the 8.5 lb dumbbell floor (rotator-cuff external rotation, scaption); (b) HORIZONTAL resistance, which gravity cannot supply (Pallof press, rotational press), plus the two knee-isolation moves the fixed-roller bench cannot do. Never prescribe a band exercise that has a dumbbell equivalent. Progress by moving further from the anchor first, then by changing colour. ONE MORE JOB, added with the Nordic pad: a band can ASSIST a movement instead of resisting it (looped over the pull-up bar and under the chest to take weight off a Nordic curl). That is not covered by the "never where a dumbbell would do" rule above — nothing else here can unload a bodyweight eccentric — and it progresses BACKWARDS: thickest band first, lighter as you get stronger.

equipment.name: Flexible resistance bar
equipment.notes: FitBeast flexible resistance bar — a solid rubber bar you BEND and TWIST (the TheraBand FlexBar pattern), not a band and not a weight. THREE bars, colour-coded: RED = 10 lb, GREEN = 15 lb, BLUE = 25 lb. The number is roughly the force needed to bend the bar into a full C, not a load you lift, and the bars carry no printed figure — ALWAYS name the COLOUR when prescribing, the way band colour is named. DELIBERATELY NARROW ROLE, same rule as the bands: dumbbells win wherever they can do the job, so this is NOT a curl, a press or a general forearm tool — wrist curls, reverse wrist curls and every carry stay on the dumbbells and the kettlebell. It is kept for the three things nothing else in the basement can do: (a) ECCENTRIC wrist-extensor loading (Tyler twist) and wrist-flexor loading (reverse Tyler twist) — the standard, well-evidenced work for tennis and golfer's elbow, which is the racquet-sport injury this gym has no other answer to; (b) resisted forearm SUPINATION / PRONATION, the rotation a pickleball stroke actually does and a dumbbell cannot load through range; (c) all of it seated, in no floor space, with no anchor. Start every twist on RED and only move to GREEN when red is easy through the full range with a slow 4-second release; BLUE is a grip bar, not a starting point. Ninety seconds of this is prehab, not a workout — never the main movement of a session.

equipment.name: Nordic curl pad
equipment.notes: A portable Nordic hamstring curl device — a padded knee board with a foot roller that pins the ankles. Sets up on the floor in seconds, no rack, no partner holding your heels. It does exactly ONE movement and there is no substitute for it in this basement: a knee-flexion ECCENTRIC with the hips locked, which is the single best-evidenced hamstring injury-prevention exercise there is, and it loads the hamstrings HARD with ZERO spinal load — the reason it matters here, where the other two hamstring options (Romanian deadlift, kettlebell swing) are both flagged backRisk. OWNER STATUS, confirmed: an unassisted Nordic is currently IMPOSSIBLE — he cannot control the descent at all. That is normal and it is not a reason to skip the movement; it is a reason to prescribe an ASSISTED version. The ladder is band-assisted → hands-catch negatives → unassisted, and it is walked in that order over months, never rushed. Never prescribe the unassisted Nordic until the assisted one is easy for 3 × 6 with a slow descent. Hips STAY EXTENDED throughout on every version — the moment the movement becomes a hip hinge it stops being a hamstring exercise and starts being a lower back one.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.how: Lie flat, dumbbells at chest level, press up until arms are straight over your chest. Keep both feet planted and don't arch the lower back off the bench.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.how: Set the backrest to 30-45 degrees, press the dumbbells from upper-chest level to straight overhead. Shoulder blades stay pinned back against the pad.

exercises.name: Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.how: Set the bench to decline and hook your legs under the padded rollers, press the dumbbells from lower chest to lockout. Sit up slowly between sets, don't jerk upright.

exercises.name: Dips
exercises.how: Support yourself on the bars, lower until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, press back up. Stop at parallel — going deeper strains the shoulder.

exercises.name: Push-ups
exercises.how: Hands under the shoulders, body in one straight line, chest to just above the floor.

exercises.name: Pull-ups
exercises.how: Hang, pull until your chin clears the bar, lower all the way down under control.

exercises.name: Chin-up
exercises.how: Hang with palms facing you, pull until your chin clears the bar. Keep ribs down so you do not arch the lower back.

exercises.name: Negative Pull-up
exercises.how: Step up to the top of the pull-up from a bench or box — do not jump. Lower yourself as slowly as you can, aiming for five seconds down. Progress by slowing the descent, then by graduating to a full pull-up.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
exercises.how: Set the backrest to about 45 degrees and lie face-down on it, row both dumbbells to your ribs. Chest stays glued to the pad the whole set.

exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.how: One hand and same-side knee on the bench, row the dumbbell to your hip. Keep the back flat and square — no twisting the torso to lift it.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.how: Backrest fully upright, sit with your back flat against it, press dumbbells from shoulder height to overhead. Keep the back on the pad — no leaning back to push.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.how: Stand tall, light dumbbells at your sides, raise them out to shoulder height with a slight elbow bend. Lead with the elbows, stop at shoulder level, lower slowly.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Reverse Fly
exercises.how: Face-down on the incline bench, light dumbbells hanging, sweep the arms out and back like opening wings. Squeeze the shoulder blades, don't shrug.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Y-Raise
exercises.how: Face-down on the incline bench with very light dumbbells, raise the arms overhead into a Y shape. Thumbs up, no shrugging, tiny weight only.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
exercises.how: Stand with dumbbells at your sides, curl up without swinging the elbows forward. Keep elbows pinned to your ribs the whole way.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
exercises.how: Curl with palms facing each other, thumbs up, elbows tight to your sides. Don't let the shoulders shrug up at the top.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.how: Set the backrest around 45 degrees, sit back with arms hanging straight down, curl up. Keep your upper arms behind your torso and shoulders pressed into the pad.

exercises.name: Lying Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.how: Lie on the bench, dumbbells above your chest, bend at the elbows to lower them beside your head. Keep the upper arms vertical and don't flare the elbows wide.

exercises.name: Seated Overhead Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.how: Sit with the backrest upright, hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands, lower it behind your head and press back up. Back stays against the pad, ribs down.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.how: Rear foot on the bench, dumbbells at your sides, drop the back knee straight down and drive up through the front heel. Keep the front shin near vertical and the torso tall.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
exercises.how: Hold dumbbells at your sides, step back and drop the rear knee toward the floor, then drive forward to stand. Stepping backwards keeps the front knee calm.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.how: Dumbbells in front of your thighs, push the hips back and slide the weights down your legs with a flat back, then stand. Stop when the hamstrings tighten, never round the back.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.how: Hold one dumbbell vertically at your chest, squat down between your knees and stand up. Elbows inside the knees, chest up, weight stays close to the body.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Lunge
exercises.how: Hold one dumbbell at your chest, step wide to one side and sit back into that hip while the other leg stays straight. Keep both feet flat and the chest up.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Step-up
exercises.how: Dumbbells at your sides, step one foot onto the bench and stand up fully without pushing off the back leg. Lower under control, don't drop down.

exercises.name: Calf Raise
exercises.how: Up on the toes as high as you can, slow all the way back down.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.how: Stand on one foot holding a dumbbell, rise onto the ball of the foot and lower slowly. Hold something for balance if needed.

exercises.name: Bench Hip Thrust
exercises.how: Upper back on the bench, dumbbell across the hips, drive hips up to a straight line. Tuck the chin and squeeze glutes at the top, no back arch.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.how: On your back, heels close to the hips, drive through the heels and squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.how: Lie on your back, one foot planted and the other leg straight up, push the hips up level. Keep the hips square — don't let one side drop.

demo.sourceName: single leg bridge with outstretched leg

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
exercises.how: Hinge and hike the bell back, then snap the hips to float it to chest height. Arms stay relaxed, the hips do the work.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.how: On all fours, extend opposite arm and leg, hold a beat, keep the hips level. Gold for the lower back.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.how: On your back, lower back glued to the floor. Extend opposite arm and leg slowly, then swap.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.how: On one forearm, hips stacked and lifted, body in a straight line. Both sides.

exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank
exercises.how: Side plank on your forearm with the top leg's inner knee or ankle resting on the bench, lift the hips. Start with the knee version; keep the body in one line.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.how: Forearms down, body in one line, ribs pulled down, squeeze everything. Hold.

exercises.name: L-Sit Hold
exercises.how: Support on the bars with arms straight, lift both legs out in front until they're level with your hips. Press the shoulders down; bend the knees if you can't hold it straight.

exercises.name: Dip Bar Knee Raise
exercises.how: Support yourself on the dip bars with straight arms and raise your knees to your chest. Keep shoulders pressed down, no swinging.

exercises.name: Suitcase Hold
exercises.how: Hold the kettlebell at one side and stand tall for time. Do not let that shoulder drop or the torso lean.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
exercises.how: A dumbbell in each hand, walk tall with the shoulders back and short quick steps. Stop when your posture breaks, not when your grip does.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl
exercises.how: Sit, rest forearms on your thighs or the bench with palms up and wrists past the edge. Curl the weight up with the hand only, no forearm movement.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Reverse Wrist Curl
exercises.how: Same seated position but palms down, wrists off the knee or bench edge. Lift the back of the hand up, go light, control the way down.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Farmer's Hold
exercises.how: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and stand tall for time. Shoulders back, ribs down.

exercises.name: Flexbar Tyler Twist
exercises.how: BAR: RED (10 lb) — start here, green only when red is easy through full range. Hold the bar upright in the WORKING hand with the wrist bent back (knuckles toward you), grab the top with the other hand palm-out. Twist the TOP hand to wind the bar up, then bring both arms out in front of you so the bar is horizontal. Now release the wound-up bar SLOWLY — four full seconds — letting the working wrist un-bend against it. The slow release is the entire exercise; winding it up is just setup. Elbow-tendon work: light, controlled, no speed.

exercises.name: Flexbar Reverse Tyler Twist
exercises.how: BAR: RED (10 lb). The mirror of the Tyler twist, for the INSIDE of the elbow. Hold the bar upright in the working hand with the wrist bent FORWARD (palm curling in), grab the top with the other hand and wind the bar up the opposite way. Arms out in front, bar horizontal, then let it unwind over four slow seconds through the working wrist. Same rule: the release is the work.

exercises.name: Flexbar Supination
exercises.how: BAR: RED or GREEN. Sit with the working forearm resting on your thigh, palm down, hand past the knee. Hold the bar upright, pin the far end with the other hand, and rotate the working palm UP against the bar's twist, then let it wind back slowly. Rotation only — the elbow stays on the leg and the shoulder does not move. This is the forearm rotation a racquet stroke lives on, and it is the one thing the dumbbells cannot load through range.

exercises.name: Split Squat Jump
exercises.how: From a split stance, jump and switch legs in the air, landing softly. Three per side. Stop the set the moment jump height, landing control or speed drops — even at two reps. Full rest between sets; never take this near failure.

exercises.name: Squat Jump
exercises.how: Drop into a shallow squat and jump as high as you can, landing soft with bent knees. Absorb every landing — no stiff legs.

exercises.name: Tuck Jump
exercises.how: Jump straight up pulling your knees toward your chest, land softly. Bend the knees on landing to absorb it.

exercises.name: Lateral Shuffle
exercises.how: Stay low in a half squat and shuffle sideways a few steps each way. Keep the chest up and feet from crossing.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
exercises.how: Stand facing a wall, ball at the chest. Drive it into the wall as hard as you can and catch the rebound. Stop the set the moment the throw slows — even at two reps. Full rest between sets.

exercises.name: Band External Rotation
exercises.how: BAND: YELLOW (lightest, 20 lb label). Anchor at elbow height. Stand side-on, working arm nearest the anchor tucked at 90° with the elbow pinned to the ribs, rotate the forearm away from the body, then back with control. Light tension only — this is cuff work.

exercises.name: Band Scaption
exercises.how: BAND: YELLOW (lightest, 20 lb label). Stand on the band. Thumbs up, raise both arms to shoulder height in the scapular plane — about 30° in front of the shoulders, not straight out to the side. Lower slowly. Light tension: it is prehab, not a lateral raise.

exercises.name: Band Leg Curl
exercises.how: BAND: BLACK (65 lb label) — PURPLE if you do both legs at once. Anchor low in front of the bench. Lie face down and loop the band around ONE ankle. Curl the heel towards the glutes against the pull, then lower slowly all the way. Keep the hips flat and do not let them rise. Both ankles at once also works when you want the set over faster — it needs roughly twice the tension, so move further from the anchor. To progress, increase the anchor distance; do not buy a heavier band.

exercises.name: Band-Assisted Nordic Curl
exercises.how: BAND: PURPLE (the thickest, most help) to start — the band here is ASSISTANCE, not resistance, so you go LIGHTER as you get stronger, the opposite of every other band exercise. Loop it over the pull-up bar or high on the post so it hangs in front of you, and pass it under your armpits across the chest. Kneel on the pad, ankles under the roller, hips locked straight so knee to shoulder is one line. Lower yourself forward as SLOWLY as you can, letting the band take whatever you cannot hold, then pull back up. Stop the set the moment the descent turns into a drop — an uncontrolled fall trains nothing. Progress by moving to a lighter band (purple → black → red), never by adding reps first.

exercises.name: Nordic Curl Negative
exercises.how: The step AFTER band-assisted, not a starting point. Kneel on the pad, ankles under the roller, hips locked straight, hands ready in front of you. Lower under control for as long as you can hold it, then CATCH yourself on your hands and push back to the top with the arms — the hamstrings only do the way down. Every session the catch should happen a little lower. Hips never hinge.

exercises.name: Nordic Curl
exercises.how: The full movement, and the top of the ladder — do not prescribe this until band-assisted is easy for 3 × 6 with a slow descent. Kneel on the pad, ankles under the roller, hips locked so knee to shoulder is one straight line. Lower all the way to the floor under hamstring control, touch down lightly with the hands, and pull yourself back up with the hamstrings. Low reps forever: this is a very high-tension movement and five good ones beat ten scrappy ones.

exercises.name: Band Leg Extension
exercises.how: BAND: PURPLE (85 lb label) — drop to BLACK if you cannot finish the set. Anchor low behind you. Sit on the bench and loop the band around ONE ankle, across the front. Straighten the knee against the pull, squeeze the quad at the top, then return under control. Both ankles at once also works and halves the time, at roughly twice the tension. To progress, move the bench further from the anchor; do not buy a heavier band.

exercises.name: Band Pallof Press
exercises.how: BAND: RED (35 lb label) — move up to BLACK when 12 reps feel easy. Anchor at chest height on the post. Stand side-on with the band held at the sternum, press it straight out and hold 2 s while the band tries to rotate you, then bring it back in. Resist the twist — nothing above the hips should move.

exercises.name: Band Rotational Press
exercises.how: BAND: RED (35 lb label) — move up to BLACK when the throw stops feeling fast. Anchor at chest height. Stand side-on, band in both hands at the chest, then rotate through the back hip and press away explosively — the pickleball drive. Return under control and reset. Speed, not grind.

exercises.name: Back Extension
exercises.how: Hips on the pad, ankles under the rollers, arms crossed on the chest. Hinge down until you feel the hamstrings, then squeeze the glutes to come back to ONE straight line — stop level, never arch past it. Slow both ways; this is endurance work, not a lift.
